---

{{< include _partials/_setup.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| include: false
# numbers quoted below, from config/model.yml and output/backtest/; "–" where a result is missing
from collections import defaultdict

design = site.design_facts()
facts = defaultdict(lambda: "–", site.backtest_facts())
probe = defaultdict(lambda: "–", site.probe_facts())
```

Every modelling choice in this project was kept or dropped on evidence from backtests: refitting the model as it
would have run before past elections, and scoring the forecasts against what happened.

## Backtest design

* **Targets.** The `{python} design["targets"]` elections.
* **Horizons.** Forecasts made `{python} design["horizons"]` weeks before each election:
  `{python} design["n_cases"]` cases per variant.
* **Information set.** Only the polls available at the cutoff, and only the results of earlier elections.
  Wikipedia records when fieldwork happened, not when a poll was published, so a poll counts once its fieldwork
  has ended and a typical publication delay for its pollster has passed (`publication_lag_days` in
  `config/pollsters.yml`: 2 days for Verian and Reid Research, 10 for Roy Morgan and Talbot Mills, 5 by default).
  The tracked parties, the pollsters kept and the fundamentals prior are all derived from that information set
  too.
* **Variants.** The 2023 model replica (`legacy`), `base`, `gauss` and `heavy`, with `{python} design["chains"]`
  chains of `{python} design["warmup"]` warmup and `{python} design["draws"]` draws each. The fundamentals variant
  was tested separately; see [below](#fundamentals-prior).

## Scores

Scores use the vote shares of the tracked parties, excluding the residual "Other" category.

| Score | What it measures | Better |
|---|---|---|
| CRPS | error of the whole forecast distribution, in percentage points; equals the absolute error for a point forecast | lower |
| Energy score | multivariate CRPS over all tracked parties jointly | lower |
| Mean absolute error | error of the forecast mean | lower |
| 90% and 50% coverage | share of party results inside the central 90% and 50% intervals | close to 0.9 and 0.5 |
| Brier score (bloc lead) | probability forecast of the right bloc winning more seats than the left bloc, using the electorates each party actually won | lower |

A log score on the log-ratio scale was tried first and rejected. Parties on 0.1% to 0.5%, such as United Future
in 2017, dominated it, although their errors do not affect seats.

## Combining variants

The published forecast is a weighted mixture of variants. The weights come from **stacking on CRPS**
(Yao, Vehtari, Simpson and Gelman 2018): choose weights $w$ on the simplex that minimise the total CRPS of the
mixture over all backtest cases. For a mixture the CRPS is a convex quadratic,

$$\text{CRPS}(w) = w^\top A - \tfrac{1}{2}\, w^\top B\, w, \qquad A_a = \mathbb{E}|X_a - y|, \quad B_{ab} = \mathbb{E}|X_a - X_b'|,$$

summed over parties and cases, and a small quadratic programme (SLSQP) finds its minimum.

The weights used for {{< var election.year >}} are fitted on `{python} facts["n_stacked"]` backtest cases:
`{python} facts["weights"]`.

To score the ensemble honestly, each election is held out in turn and its weights are fitted on the other
elections only (`{python} facts["loeo"]`). The equal-weight mixture of the candidates is scored for comparison.

## Spread calibration

A common post-processing step (EMOS, Gneiting and others 2005) rescales a forecast's spread by a factor learned
from past errors. Here the factor is $c(h) = \exp(a + b \log h)$ for a forecast $h$ weeks out, applied on the
log-ratio scale about the mixture mean, and fitted by minimising CRPS. It is evaluated with nested hold-outs:
when an election is held out, neither the spread factor nor the stacking weights inside its training mixtures
see that election's result.

Out of sample, the calibrated ensemble scored a CRPS of `{python} facts["calibrated_crps"]` against
`{python} facts["ensemble_crps"]` without calibration, and its 90% coverage `{python} facts["shortest"]` out was
`{python} facts["calibrated_cov_short"]` against `{python} facts["ensemble_cov_short"]`. It is off
(`forecast.calibrate_spread`).

## Results

These tables are rebuilt from `output/backtest/` every time the site is built.

{{< include _partials/_backtest-tables.qmd >}}

* The ensemble's CRPS is `{python} facts["crps_gain"]` lower than the 2023 model's, and it scored better in
  `{python} facts["n_better"]` of the `{python} facts["n_compared"]` cases where both were run. The 2023 model was better in
  `{python} facts["legacy_wins"]`.
* The biggest gain is calibration. The 2023 model's 90% intervals held `{python} facts["legacy_cov90"]` of
  results, against `{python} facts["ensemble_cov90"]` for the ensemble: its fixed sample size and very smooth
  random walk made it overconfident.
* On the bloc-lead question the 2023 model's Brier score was `{python} facts["legacy_brier"]`, against
  `{python} facts["ensemble_brier"]` for the ensemble. It was confidently right in all three elections, partly
  because its smooth path barely reacted to Labour's surge after Jacinda Ardern became leader in 2017. Three
  elections cannot separate that from luck.
* The Gaussian variants beat the Dirichlet-multinomial one, which stacking all but ignores. The Gaussian and
  heavy-tailed variants are too close for three elections to rank.

### Fundamentals prior

Forecasting `{python} probe["target"]` `{python} probe["weeks"]` weeks out, the Gaussian variant scored a CRPS of
`{python} probe["crps_without"]` points without the fundamentals prior and `{python} probe["crps_with"]` with it.
The prior moved `{python} probe["pm"]` to `{python} probe["pm_with"]`, against `{python} probe["pm_without"]`
without it; `{python} probe["pm"]` won `{python} probe["pm_result"]`. The prior is anchored on the Prime
Minister's party's previous result, which in 2020 was a landslide. It is excluded from the ensemble.

## Limitations

* **Three elections.** Twelve cases sound like more than they are: forecasts of the same election at different
  horizons share its surprises. Differences of a few percent in CRPS between variants are not meaningful.
* **Electorates are not tested.** The bloc-lead score uses the electorates each party actually won, so it tests
  the vote forecast only. The {{< var election.year >}} electorate assumptions in `config/electorates.yml` are
  editorial.
* **Publication delays are approximate**, so a backtest may occasionally include a poll a day or two before it
  was published, or exclude one after.
* **Single-poll pollsters are dropped** (`min_polls: 2`), for example Anacta in 2026.

The backtests are rerun from GitHub Actions on request. How to run them yourself is in the
[operations guide](https://github.com/ariedotcodotnz/nz-poll-of-polls/blob/main/docs/operations.md), and the
files they write are described in the
[outputs guide](https://github.com/ariedotcodotnz/nz-poll-of-polls/blob/main/docs/outputs.md).
